## Graphql

- [Integration Guides Overview](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides): The integration guides are designed to give you context and guidance on implementing specific features of the GraphQL API.

- [Apple Pay](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/apple_pay/): [Apple Pay](https://developer.apple.com/apple-pay/) is a mobile and online purchasing experience for customers with supported iOS and macOS devices.

- [Overview](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/paypal/overview/): You can use the Braintree-GraphQL APIs alone and integrate PayPal as a payment method to accept payments from your customer's PayPal account.
- [One-time payments](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/paypal/one-time-payments/): You can set up one-time payments to process a buyer’s single-immediate payment through PayPal without storing the payment method for future use.
- [Checkout-with-vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/paypal/checkout-with-vault/): You can set up checkout-with-vault payments to process a payer’s immediate payment through PayPal and save the payment method for future transactions.
- [Vaulted payments](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/paypal/vaulted-payments/): You can set up vaulted payments to: 1. Save the payer’s PayPal payment method credentials for future transactions without processing an immediate payment.

- [Brazil Billing Agreement with Installments Overview](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/financing_options/): Consumers using credit cards in Brazil are accustomed to seeing installment options to pay for some or all of the items in their shopping cart.

- [Local Payment Contexts](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/local_payment_contexts/): To retrieve info about a Local Payment Context, you need its global ID. If you have an ID in a legacy UUID format, convert it first to its global format with a GraphQL query.
